headline: Anthropic researcher reports Claude-assisted full-sky ultraviolet map with prediction provenance
summary: Johns Hopkins astrophysicist and Anthropic researcher Brice Ménard reports using Claude Science and coordinated agents to harmonize ultraviolet observations from GALEX, Swift-UVOT, FIMS/SPEAR and TD-1, add Gaia-derived stellar estimates, and create an all-sky map. The author-hosted technical page says remaining gaps are filled by statistical regression and labels each pixel by provenance; it reports typical held-out errors of about 0.05–0.06 dex for predicted diffuse sky. Roughly one quarter to one third of the sky remains model-predicted depending on band and provenance layer, and the paper is marked in preparation. These are author-reported results; the downloadable data and code are not yet available on the page.
